solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Water pipe close to basin in loo

indicators.note: the closing letter of basin is placed inside the word for loo

parts.note: bog is British slang for a lavatory

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A plumbing complaint: some pipe near the washbasin in the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A water pipe for smoking, where the smoke bubbles through water, is a well-known slang term for this device.

clue.text: Some food that's gone bad, almost entirely

parts.note: food that has gone bad is said to be off

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: entirely means all, as in 'all done'

explanation.surface: A complaint that most of a meal has spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal, the organ meats of an animal, is one kind of food, so 'some food' is a broad example definition.

clue.text: Relative and relations on ecstasy and the hard stuff?

parts.note: a gran, or grandmother, is a relative
'it' is a coy word for sexual relations
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A family gathering fuelled by drugs and strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hard stuff' suggests spirits, but here it means a very hard rock; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough igneous rock used for kerbs and worktops is literally hard material, a playful definition by description.

clue.text: Cracked ceramic pots ultimately retro from 50 AD

indicators.note: cracked suggests something broken into pieces, so the following letters are reassembled
pots, as in gone to pot, adds to the sense that the pottery's letters are broken up and reworked
ultimately takes the closing letters of the words retro and from

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An antiques description: broken pottery in a retro style dating from the first century.
explanation.walkthrough: '50 AD' reads as a date, but 50 is the Roman L and AD is the definition, short for advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: On television or radio an advertisement break is filled with these paid spots, so the abbreviation is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Side with Democrat over zealous Trump base?

parts.note: a camp is a side or faction in a dispute
D is the standard abbreviation for a US Democrat
avid means keen or zealous

explanation.surface: A US political jibe about siding with Democrats over Trump's fervent supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump base' suggests his voters; here it is a physical base used by US presidents, Trump among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maryland country retreat of US presidents is literally a base any president, Trump included, may use.

clue.text: One cutting up fish waiter served after Mexican starter

indicators.note: after puts the angler word behind the opening letter
a starter is the first course, so the first letter of Mexican is taken

parts.note: an angler is someone who waits for fish to bite

explanation.surface: A restaurant scene: a fish dish served by a waiter after a Mexican starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish waiter' looks like a restaurant server; it is someone waiting on a riverbank for a bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mangles things hacks and mutilates them, so a mangler is one who cuts things up badly.

clue.text: European surgeon rings head of news to get result

indicators.note: rings means surrounds, so the surgeon word encircles the next letter

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A European surgeon telephones the newsdesk chief to report an outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: An event can mean an outcome, as in the phrase 'in the event', so it is a synonym for result.

clue.text: Punters caught out by current in fast bit of stream

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in places the current symbol inside the fast word

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: a bit of the word stream is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Anglers or bathers swept away by a strong current in a fast-flowing stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Punters is British informal usage for customers, so it is a synonym for those who buy a service.

clue.text: One starting Roger's gas off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s counts here as a letter

explanation.surface: Roger's gas supply has been cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of Roger's is needed as a letter of the fodder; 'starting' means starting a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressor is the party who begins a fight or war, the one who starts the hostilities.

clue.text: Gang firmer with one redeploying scare tactics

indicators.note: redeploying means arranging forces afresh, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A crime gang becomes tougher by putting one member to work on intimidation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading alarm to manipulate people is the practice of a scaremonger, a term for scare tactics used to sway opinion.

clue.text: After initial loss, got going again in league

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: rallied means recovered or got going again

explanation.surface: A sports team bounced back after losing their first match in the league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In league' looks like part of the sports story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Countries in league with each other are joined by alliance, as wartime partners were.

clue.text: Having stopped inventions, I flog catalogues

indicators.note: the following pieces have stopped, that is plugged, the lies word by sitting inside it

parts.note: lies are fabrications or inventions
tan means to beat or thrash, as in 'tan your hide'

explanation.surface: An inventor who has given up inventing now sells catalogues instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Litanies are long tedious lists, as in a litany of complaints, so they are catalogues in that sense.

clue.text: Old type starting court action bringing in black witness

indicators.note: bringing in means the letter is taken inside the other pieces

parts.note: a server is the type of person who starts play on a tennis court
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned legal type launches a case that involves a black witness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court action' suggests law, but it is a tennis court and the server starts each point.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer is someone who sees what happens, so it is a synonym for a witness.

clue.text: Highly enjoyable fair

definitions.meaning: something lovely and delightful, as in a wonderful day
fair in its old sense of lovely to look at, as in 'fair maiden'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both delightful in experience and good-looking, matching both senses of the clue's two definitions.

clue.text: To some extent, jackass is terrible help

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grumble that some idiot is really no help at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist someone is to give them a hand, so it is a straight synonym for help.

clue.text: A dire path taken about divisive foreign policy

indicators.note: taken about suggests being turned around and reordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A government takes a disastrous route on foreign affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: South Africa's former system of racial segregation was a policy that divided people, foreign to British readers.

clue.text: Way in which one's visiting A&E in relief

indicators.note: in which says the other letters sit inside the way abbreviation

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

indicators.note: visiting means going inside, so this piece sits within the hospital letters

parts.note: A&E is the British hospital accident and emergency department
one is I, and the 's is IS, giving I plus IS

explanation.surface: Someone describes being relieved after a trip to the hospital casualty department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is Britain's accident and emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: Carving in relief stands out from its background, so a design in relief is one that is raised.

clue.text: Time without a partner initially is top

parts.note: single means unattached, without a partner

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word Time

explanation.surface: A dating lament: a period without a partner is the best time.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest worn on the upper body, a kind of top in clothing.

clue.text: Unscrupulous opportunist heading for youth court

parts.note: a chancer is British slang for an opportunist who takes risks dishonestly

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A young chancer is on his way to the youth court.
explanation.walkthrough: Chancer is British slang for a shifty opportunist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancery Division is one of the divisions of the English High Court, so this is a court.

clue.text: Conservative sullen about a new glasnost, perhaps

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer pieces surround the inner

parts.note: dour means gloomy or sullen

explanation.surface: A grumpy Tory is complaining about a new openness policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasnost was the Soviet policy of openness, an example of frankness, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: State spies detaining Oscar-winning singer

indicators.note: detaining means holding inside, so the spy agency surrounds the rest

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

indicators.note: winning means taking in, so the singer word gains the letter

parts.note: a rat is an informer, one who sings to the police
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Intelligence agents hold an award-winning vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' suggests a performer; it is a criminal who sings, that is informs.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a Balkan country, an example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: Risk-taker likely to get a break in Hollywood?

definitions.text: Risk-taker likely to get a break in Hollywood?

parts.words: Risk-taker likely to get a break in Hollywood?
parts.note: a big break is a lucky start in films, but here the break is a broken bone suffered doing dangerous scenes

explanation.definitionFit: A film double who performs dangerous falls and crashes takes risks and may break a bone in the process.

clue.text: Medium-sized fruit with eaten-away core in wood

parts.note: M is the clothing size medium

indicators.note: the core of the fruit word, one of its middle letters, is removed

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: A mid-sized apple eaten to the core found in a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple is the timber of the maple tree, used for furniture, so it is a kind of wood.

clue.text: Recurring ideas in class about cribbing exercises

indicators.note: cribbing means taking or holding, so the reversed word encloses the exercises
about means turned around, so the class word is read backwards

parts.note: a sort is a kind or class
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A school class copies each other's exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cribbing' suggests cheating; here it means holding something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropes are recurring themes or motifs in literature and film, ideas that keep coming back.

clue.text: What houses paintings in our place?

indicators.note: houses means holds inside, so the exclamation encloses the art word

parts.note: eh is an exclamation meaning what?
art means paintings collectively

explanation.surface: A question about where at home the paintings are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' looks like the question word opening the riddle; it is the exclamation eh.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet humans live on is our home in the cosmos, so 'our place' defines it.

clue.text: One might cast Oscar-winner with thin skin on job with men

parts.note: a film is a thin layer or skin
a project is a piece of work or job
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers, men

explanation.surface: Casting a thin-skinned award-winning star on a job with men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests choosing actors; here it means throwing images onto a screen, and the Oscar-winner is a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: This machine throws moving images onto a screen, so it casts a movie such as an Academy Award winner.

clue.text: Insensitive old teacher needs retraining

indicators.note: retraining reshapes something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insensitive veteran teacher needs to go back on a course.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tone-deaf or tactless, unable to pick up on nuance, is a British informal sense of this term.

clue.text: Store that doesn't open for long

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store

explanation.surface: A shop that doesn't open for long hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as a length of time but is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn or pine, the same sense as longing for it.
